Home Depot stock faces test as housing hopes outrun store demand
sum: Home Depot stock is heading into its November 17 third-quarter update with a stronger market backdrop but unresolved questions about store demand. A Yahoo Finance analysis published Thursday, November 5 said the shares had risen 12 percent in the week through November 4 as investors priced in possible housing support and lower mortgage rates after the U.S. midterm elections.

Home Depot stock traded at 319.75 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 14:10 CET on Thursday, November 5, 6.39 percent above the Xetra close of Wednesday, November 4. The real-time quote of Home Depot stock provides the latest market indication.

The company’s second-quarter figures showed why investors still need confirmation from the operating business. Sales increased 5.7 percent to 47.9 billion dollars, but 1.4 billion dollars of the 2.6 billion dollar increase came from the GMS acquisition. Comparable customer transactions declined 1.0 percent, while the average ticket increased 2.8 percent as shoppers concentrated on smaller projects.

That mix leaves larger renovation demand exposed to housing conditions. U.S. home sales were running at an annualized 3.99 million pace in September, down 2.2 percent from a year earlier, according to the Yahoo Finance analysis. The report said analysts cited in the article remained doubtful that new housing aid would become law, while the decline in the 10-year Treasury yield after the midterms was limited.

Management’s fiscal-year outlook calls for adjusted earnings per share to be flat to 4 percent higher than the 14.69 dollars reported last year. Analysts cited by Yahoo Finance placed normalized earnings near 15.02 dollars for the year and expected growth of about 6 percent in the following year.

The November 17 call will therefore focus on whether customer transactions improve and whether management maintains its outlook for comparable sales growth of flat to 2 percent this year. A stronger housing market could eventually support larger projects, but the current store data still point to cautious consumer behavior.
The next scheduled company event is Home Depot’s third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday, November 17.

Apple, Home Depot and GE Vernova Object to ICE-OKX Tokenized Stock Venue as Count Hits 59
sum: Apple, The Home Depot and GE Vernova have objected to having tokenized versions of their shares traded on OKXICE TSV, the planned onchain stock venue owned by Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) and OKX, according to a public notice the venue dated Nov. 3.

The notice names 59 issuers that have sent it a notice of issuer objection. By Unchained's count of the venue's earlier filings, that compares with 56 in the Nov. 2 notice and 50 in the Oct. 30 notice, and no company has been removed from the list in that time. Like the earlier versions, the Nov. 3 filing does not say why any company objected, and it sets no date for trading to begin.

On Nov. 2, citing the 50 objectors in the Oct. 30 notice, Zero Knowledge Group founder Austin Campbell said on Unchained's Bits + Bips that "people are just objecting as soon as they find out about this thing." Lumida Wealth founder Ram Ahluwalia said on the same episode, "I don't know what's being solved by tokenizing a stock on chain."
The three new names join a roster that already included Microsoft, Alphabet, Nvidia, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Tesla, Amazon and SpaceX.

The notice says the venue may list stocks tokenized by their issuer or by a third party unaffiliated with the issuer. An objection keeps third-party tokens of that company's shares off the venue. Andrew Cuomo, who co-chairs the joint venture, told reporters on Oct. 29 that objections now come in on a rolling basis. "The start period has passed. There's no end period," he said.

OKXICE LLC, a Texas company that ICE and OKC USA Holding Inc. own in equal halves, runs the venue under the SEC exemption for tokenized securities venues, published in the Federal Register on Sept. 22. Trades will settle in permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on XLayer, and only wallets holding a soulbound token issued by the venue can use them.

The notice states that the venue is "not registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission" for this activity and has no policies addressing maximal extractable value. Its hook contract is to be audited by OKX Technology Inc. and by Certified Kernel Tech LLC before operations start.

sum: - Home-improvement bluechip stays central to market attention

Home Depot (NYSE:HD) Consumer Cyclical The Home Depot Inc (NYSE:HD) 340.50 USD +11.300 3.433% Last Updated at: 2026-11-02T21:04:00Z has stayed firmly in market focus today as shifting housing conditions and renovation demand frame attention toward the home-improvement bluechip during an earnings-heavy stretch. As 1 of the largest retailers serving homeowners and building professionals alike, the company sits at the crossroads of housing activity, repair spending and the broader health of the American household. The name continues to stand out among Bluechip Stocks tracked across the US market.

The attention comes during a week when consumer-facing and housing-linked names draw particular scrutiny. Because the home-improvement space reflects both the mood of homeowners and the pace of construction and repair work, the company serves as a useful barometer of how willing households are to commit to larger projects. Reporting from finance outlets has centered on how renovation demand is tracking as conditions in the housing market continue to evolve.

The housing backdrop shapes much of how the home-improvement space is understood. The stock is a constituent of the [Dow Jones Industrial Average], S&P 500, NYSE Composite and Russell 1000, which keeps it within the reach of index-tracking funds. When conditions in the housing market firm, activity around renovations, repairs and upgrades tends to follow, while a cooler backdrop can prompt homeowners to delay larger projects. The current period has placed this relationship in sharp focus as the market weighs how the housing environment is shifting.

A central feature of the current backdrop is the tension between a cautious rate environment and the enduring need for maintenance and repair. Even when conditions prompt households to defer major remodeling, essential upkeep continues, which lends the home-improvement space a measure of steadiness. Homes require ongoing care regardless of the broader mood, and that durable demand anchors the sector through varied conditions.
Professional customers form a distinctive and important part of the home-improvement story.

What Is The True Hidden Price Of Home Depot Stock?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Home Depot (HD) trades at 22.3 times its last twelve months of adjusted earnings (normalized net income plus after-tax stock pay). That is a steep price for a company reporting less profit than it did four years ago. You pay for future profit, however, making it useful to weigh this price against expected profit for the next two fiscal years. So what does that same price buy on the profit ahead?

Based on the consensus forecast, Home Depot trades at 21.9 times expected profit for fiscal 2027, the year now under way, and 20.7 times expected profit for fiscal 2028. (Years here are named for the calendar year in which they end, meaning the period Home Depot refers to as fiscal 2026 is fiscal 2027 here.) This indicates the hidden price of Home Depot stock is still more than 20 times profit, whether you count the last twelve months or either forecast year.

For those multiples to be what you actually pay, Home Depot must grow sales near the top of its guidance and slightly widen its margin. The consensus forecast puts fiscal 2027 sales at $172 billion, up from $165 billion in fiscal 2026. That represents growth of about 4%, approaching the high end of the 2.5% to 4.5% range management guided in August for the same year.

For fiscal 2028, the forecast calls for sales to grow another 3.4%, outpacing the 2.5% rate Home Depot delivered over the last twelve months. While total sales rose 5.7% in the latest quarter, comparable sales increased only 1.7%. Management said its fiscal 2027 guidance for total sales growth reflects the GMS acquisition, new stores, new branches and tuck-in acquisitions, meaning not all of that growth comes from comparable sales.

The consensus forecast also models an 8.9% net margin in fiscal 2028, compared with the 8.6% Home Depot reported for fiscal 2026. This would lift net income to $15.8 billion in fiscal 2028, up from the $14.2 billion reported in fiscal 2026. That wider margin remains an assumption, not a result.
Sales are one area where the forecast could prove too high. Management guided comparable sales growth of flat to 2% for fiscal 2027.

sum: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after major indices pulled back and retail equities faced pressure as the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported a hotter-than-expected September inflation print, pushing Treasury yields higher.

As detailed by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the consumer price index rose 3.7% year-over-year in September, topping the 3.6% estimate from economists polled by Dow Jones. According to CNBC, core inflation—which excludes volatile food and energy costs—climbed 2.6% annually against expectations of 2.5%, largely bolstered by a 9.1% surge in gasoline costs and higher expenses for air travel. Following the print, CNBC market data showed the 10-year Treasury yield climbed over six basis points to 5.278%, while the 30-year yield advanced past 5.59%. According to market commentators, rising yields intensify pressure on equity valuations and consumer spending power just as third-quarter corporate earnings get underway.

In remarks carried by CNBC, Franklin Templeton Institute head investment strategist Jeff Schulze noted that pressure across the long end of the curve acts as a valuation headwind for risk assets. Financial analysts explain that higher benchmark yields mechanically elevate the discount rate applied to corporate earnings, compressing the multiples investors are willing to pay for consumer discretionary and retail equities.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

sum: As the consumer landscape evolves, investors must choose between high-growth disruptors and established dividend payers. We compare Carvana (CVNA -7.07%) and Home Depot (HD -1.55%) to see which stock offers the best path forward.

Carvana focuses on transforming the car-buying experience through an online-only model, while Home Depot provides essential materials for the housing market. Both companies rely on consumer spending but face very different hurdles. This comparison evaluates their financial health, growth trajectories, and current valuations to help you navigate these two unique opportunities.

Carvana is a prominent player among consumer discretionary stocks that focuses on transforming the car-buying experience. It operates an e-commerce platform that allows customers to buy, sell, and finance used vehicles entirely online with home delivery or local pickup. The company recently expanded its reach by acquiring seven franchised dealerships from Stellantis, marking a strategic move into the new-car market and franchised operations.

In FY 2025, the company generated revenue of nearly $20.3 billion, which represents growth of approximately 48.6% compared to the prior year. This rapid expansion supported a net income of close to $1.4 billion for the fiscal year, a significant improvement from previous years. The resulting net margin was roughly 6.9% for the period, which highlights how much profit remains after all operating costs and taxes are paid.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 1.6x. This figure represents total debt relative to shareholder equity, providing insight into the company's financial leverage and reliance on borrowed capital. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term obligations using current assets, stands at approximately 4.3x. Free cash flow reached nearly $889.0 million in FY 2025, representing the cash a company generates after accounting for capital expenditures.
Home Depot is the world's largest home improvement retailer, serving both individual homeowners and professional contractors across the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

Shares of Costco have gained +10.4% over the year-to-date period against the Zacks Retail - Discount Stores industry's gain of +14.8%. The company remains well-positioned due to its differentiated membership-based warehouse model, strong value proposition and loyal customer base. It continues to benefit from recurring membership income, high renewal rates and growing engagement from higher-value members. Its focus on offering quality merchandise at competitive prices supports steady traffic and reinforces customer loyalty.
Costco is also enhancing its digital ecosystem through e-commerce, personalization tools, AI-driven product discovery and convenient fulfillment options, helping improve the member experience.

Also, the company is expanding its warehouse footprint and investing in productivity-enhancing initiatives to support long-term growth. Backed by a strong balance sheet, Costco is well-positioned to strengthen its market leadership and drive sustainable growth over time.
